editorial:
Imagine growing up in a house where the biggest personality is someone who isn't even there. You follow a young boy who feels like a ghost in his own home because his parents are obsessed with his missing older brother from the war. It is a strange mix of a sad family story and some light comedy that keeps you interested. You get to see how a kid tries to get attention when his parents are stuck in the past, making the whole vibe feel very relatable even if you didn't live through a war.

The acting is the best part here because the kids feel real and not like they are reading from a script. The story moves at a steady pace, though some parts feel a bit slow. If you like heartfelt stories about family secrets, you will love this.
endingExplained: At the end, the boy finally forces his parents to stop living in the shadow of the missing brother. They realize that by chasing a memory, they are losing the son who is actually right in front of them. The movie wraps up with the family starting to heal and accepting the truth about the past. It is a sweet conclusion that shows the parents finally giving the young boy the love and attention he deserves.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves touching family stories and historical dramas.
similarMovies: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas
